description: Evergreen or rarely deciduous trees or shrubs, with spiral primary branching; bark longitudinally striate or cracked into plates, rarely loose and longitudinally fissured. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves coriaceous to chartaceous, mostly elliptic to lanceolate or rarely oblong to ovate, base symmetrical or rarely asymmetrical, cuneate, rounded, cordate or rarely attenuate, midrib plane or sunken above, prominent below, secondary venation indistinct, usually not prominent, tertiary venation reticulate, forming a loose or close network. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or internodal, 1–20-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, conical in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, connate at base or free, much shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, mostly triangular-ovate to ovate, subequal or inner petals slightly shorter and narrower than outer petals, base expanded, saccate, apex reflexed at anthesis, outer petals spreading to strongly revolute and inner petals erect. Stamens 12–65, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex miliusoid (not covering anther thecae), apiculate. Carpels 1–15, stigmas U-shaped to globose; ovules few to many per ovary, biseriate. Receptacle conical, hairy. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, up to 8 per fruit, yellow, dull green or pale orange when mature, cylindrical, ellipsoid, ovoid or globose, glabrous or pubescent, smooth or verrucose, stipitate or subsessile; pericarp thick, leathery or woody when dried. Seeds attached laterally in 2 rows, up to 16 per monocarp, not separating from endocarp, smooth or wrinkled, glabrous, pale brown to dark brown, perichalazal ring raised, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>A tropical Asian genus of about 38 species, bearing small flowers with saccate petals, reflexed at the tips, and miliusoid stamens; 17 species are represented in Thailand.

description: Tree ca 15 m tall; bark greyish brown, longitudinally striate. Twigs densely covered with brown appressed hairs when young, later moderately to sparsely hairy. Leaves subcoriaceous to coriaceous, oblong, elliptic, oblong-elliptic or lanceolate-oblong, 15–22 by 5–8 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or caudate, the acumen 10–20 mm long, margins revolute, glabrous, except densely hairy at base above, glabrous to sparsely hairy, with moderate to dense appressed hairs on midrib below, midrib plane above, secondary veins 7–12 per side, tertiary venation on lower surface forming a loose network; petioles 5–10 mm long. Inflorescences 1–3-flowered, peduncle 2–10 mm long, pedicels 10–15 mm long, each bearing a single bract near base; buds conical. Sepals connate at base to near midpoint, ovate, 1.5–2 mm long, obtuse. Outer petals brownish yellow, triangular-ovate to ovate, 12–16 by 6–8.5 mm, apex obtuse, hairy on both sides. Inner petals creamy white to whitish yellow, triangular-ovate, 12–17 by 7.5–9.5 mm, apex acute, hairy outside, glabrous, sometimes sparsely hairy at apex, inside. Stamens 42–52, oblong-elliptic to oblong, 0.8–1.2 mm long. Carpels 11–13, ovaries oblong, 2–3 mm long. Fruit of 2–6 monocarps borne on a pedicel 15–20 mm long. Monocarps yellow, ellipsoid, ovoid, ovoid-ellipsoid or globose, 1.5–3.5 by 1.5–2.3 cm, smooth, densely brown-hairy, with a longitudinal groove on one side, with 2–7 raised rings of transverse ridges on monocarp when dried, apex rounded, base contracted into a stipe 8–25 mm long. Seeds 2–8 per monocarp, ellipsoid-ovoid or reniform-ovoid, 8–15 by 5–8 mm.

Outer petals greenish yellow to yellow, triangular-ovate or elliptic-ovate, 8–13 by 5–6 mm, apex obtuse, hairy on both sides. Inner petals greenish yellow to yellow, triangular-elliptic, 8–10 by 3–4 mm, apex acute to obtuse, hairy outside, glabrous to sparsely hairy at apex inside. Monocarps cylindrical, oblongoid or ellipsoid, (1.5–)3–5 by 1–2.5 cm, verrucose, with dense brown hairs, apex apiculate, base contracted into a stipe 2–6 mm long. description: Tree 4–15 m tall; bark brown, longitudinally striate. Twigs glabrous to sparsely covered with brown appressed hairs when young, later glabrous. Leaves subcoriaceous to coriaceous, elliptic, oblong, lanceolate-elliptic or oblong-lanceolate, 6–20 by 2.5–7.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, the acumen 5–20 mm long, or acute, margins revolute, glabrous above, glabrous or sometimes sparsely hairy on midrib below, midrib plane above, secondary veins 8–14 per side, tertiary venation on lower surface forming a loose network; petioles 3–10 mm long. Inflorescences 1–3-flowered, peduncle 5–10 mm long, pedicels 7–15 mm long, each bearing a single bract near base; buds conical. Sepals connate at base, ovate, 1.5–2 mm long, obtuse. Outer petals creamy white to whitish yellow, triangular-ovate, 6–10 by 4–6 mm, apex obtuse, hairy on both sides, but denser on inside than on outside. Inner petals creamy white to whitish yellow, triangular-elliptic, 7–12 by 3.5–5.5 mm, apex acute to obtuse, hairy outside, glabrous to hairy on margin and at apex inside. Stamens 25–30, ovate, elliptic, or oblong-elliptic, 0.8–1.5 mm long. Carpels 3–4, ovaries oblong, 2–3 mm long. Fruit of 2–4 monocarps borne on a pedicel 25–30 mm long. Monocarps ovoid, ellipsoid or cylindrical-ellipsoid, 0.8–2 by 0.7–1 cm, smooth, with a longitudinal groove on outer surface, constricted between seeds when dried, covered with sparse brown hairs or glabrous, apex apiculate, base contracted into a stipe 1.5–3 mm long. Seeds unknown.

description: Shrub to tree 1–8 m tall; bark brown, blackish brown, or greyish brown, longitudinally striate to cracked into plates. Twigs sparsely covered with brown appressed hairs or glabrous. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, elliptic to ovate or oblong-elliptic, 3–12 by 1.5–4.5 cm, base rounded, apex acute or acuminate, the acumen 3–10 mm long, or obtuse, margins flat, glabrous or with very sparse brown hairs above, glabrous, sometimes with sparse long brown hairs on midrib or margins below, midrib plane above, secondary veins 7–13 per side, tertiary venation on lower surface forming a close network; petioles 2–6 mm long. Inflorescences 1–4-flowered, peduncle 1.5–3.5 mm long, pedicels 5–15 mm long, each bearing a single bract near midpoint or toward base; buds broadly conical. Sepals connate to the midpoint, broadly ovate, 1.2–2 mm long, obtuse. Outer petals greenish yellow or yellow, triangular-ovate or ovate, 11–15 by 6–7 mm, apex obtuse, hairy on both sides except glabrous at base inside. Inner petals greenish yellow to whitish yellow, triangular-ovate or triangular-elliptic, 11–14 by 4.5–6.5 mm, apex obtuse to slightly acute, hairy outside, glabrous to sparsely hairy at apex inside. Stamens 15–22, ovate, elliptic or oblong-elliptic, 0.8–1.6 mm long. Carpels (2–)3–5, ovaries oblong or elliptic-oblong, 2–3.5 mm long. Fruit of (2–)3–4 monocarps borne on a pedicel 7–20 mm long. Monocarps cylindrical, ellipsoid or ovoid, 1.5–4 by 1–2.5 cm, smooth, sometimes with a longitudinal groove on outer surface, irregularly constricted between seeds when dried, densely brown-hairy, apex rounded, sessile or base contracted into a stipe 2–5 mm long. Seeds not seen.

description: Tree 8–15 m tall; bark brown to blackish brown, longitudinally striate to slightly cracked into plates. Twigs glabrous to sparsely covered with brown appressed hairs when young, later glabrous to sparsely hairy. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, oblong, lanceolate, oblong-lanceolate or elliptic-lanceolate, 7–25 by 2–7 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, the acumen 10–25 mm long, margins revolute, glabrous above, glabrous or sometimes with sparse hairs below, midrib plane above, secondary veins 9–14 per side, tertiary venation on lower surface forming a loose network; petioles 3.5–10 mm long. Inflorescences 1–3-flowered, peduncle 1.5–3 mm long, pedicels 5–7 mm long, each bearing a single bract near midpoint; buds conical. Sepals connate at base, ovate, 1–2 mm long, obtuse. Outer petals greenish yellow, triangular-ovate, 10–12 by 5–8 mm, apex obtuse, hairy outside, glabrous on lower half and hairy on upper half inside. Inner petals greenish yellow to whitish yellow, ovate-triangular, 9.5–11 by 4.5–7 mm, apex obtuse to acute, hairy on margin and upper half and glabrous on lower half outside, glabrous except hairy at apex inside. Stamens 22–25, oblong, 0.8–1.2 mm long. Carpels 1(–2), ovaries oblong, 2.5–3 mm long. Fruit of 1(–2) monocarps borne on a pedicel 15–27 mm long. Monocarps cylindrical to ellipsoid, smooth, 4–9 by 3–5 cm, smooth, with a longitudinal ridge on outer surface, glabrous or sometimes with very sparse brown hairs, apex rounded, base contracted into a stipe 5–15 mm long. Seeds 8–16 per monocarp, ellipsoid, 15–25 by 8–15 mm.

description: Evergreen shrubs or small trees, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves subcoriaceous to chartaceous, mostly elliptic to oblong, base symmetrical, cuneate to rounded; midrib plane or slightly sunken above, secondary venation brochidodromous, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences terminal or leaf-opposed, 1–5-flowered, plants sometimes cauliflorous. Flowers hermaphroditic, ovoid or globose in bud. Sepals (2–)3, valvate, minutely connate at base, much shorter than petals, hairy outside, glabrous inside. Petals in two whorls of 3, or inner petals absent, valvate, free, outer petals erect to slightly spreading at anthesis, thickened, upper part on inner side flattened, bifacial to keeled, inner petals erect at anthesis, subequal or slightly shorter, narrower and sometimes with a clawed base, inner side bifacial to keeled in upper part. Stamens 15–88, innermost sometimes staminodial, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex apiculate or obtuse. Carpels few to many, stigmas U-shaped; ovules 2 per ovary, sub-basal, collateral. Receptacle convex. Fruit apocarpous, monocarps adaxially dehiscent, clavate, pubescent to glabrescent in age, smooth, often with an persistent apical beak, long-stipitate; pericarp thick, woody or leathery when dried. Seeds sub-basal or attached at base, 1–2 per monocarp, obovoid, asymmetrical, outer side convex, inner side flattened, pointed at base, smooth, shiny, black, perichalazal ring not evident, aril absent, endosperm ruminations oblique, irregularly ribbon-shaped.</br></br>A tropical genus unique in the family for the explosive dehiscence of its monocarps. About 23 species in the Neotropics and 3 native to Asia; 2 species occur in Thailand, one with 2 varieties.

description: Shrub to tree 2–8 m tall. Twigs greyish brown to brown, markedly to slightly angled in cross-section, sparsely hairy or glabrous. Leaves subcoriaceous to chartaceous, oblong, elliptic-oblong, elliptic, obovate or obovate-oblong, 8–20 cm by 3–8 cm, base slightly acute or rounded, apex obtuse to acuminate, the acumen 3–20 mm long, glabrous on both surfaces, midrib plane to slightly sunken above, secondary veins 6–12 per side; petioles 5–12 mm long, glabrous. Inflorescences terminal or leaf-opposed, 1–5-flowered, or plants cauliflorous, peduncles 3–10 mm long, pedicels 5–20 mm long; buds ovoid or globose. Sepals ovate or triangular-ovate, 4–6 mm long, obtuse to acute. Outer petals pale green to white, ovate-triangular or ovate, 12–25 mm by 8–14 mm, inner side varying from bifacial just below apex to bifacial or broadly keeled in upper third to upper half, slightly to strongly thickened toward apex, apex obtuse or acute, sparsely hairy to glabrous outside, glabrous inside. Inner petals present or absent (in var. tripetala), white, elliptic-rhomboid, 7–22 mm by 4–10 mm, inner side bifacial to broadly keeled in upper third, concave at middle part of inner side, apex acute to acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces. Stamens 37–88, spatulate, 2.5–4 mm long, plus 10–25 staminodes. Carpels 3–16, ovaries oblong or linear-oblong, 1.7–2 mm long. Fruit of 1–16 monocarps borne on a pedicel 10–20 mm long. Monocarps brown to blackish brown at maturity, 2.5–3.5 cm by 0.7–1 cm, persistent apical beak straight, 0.1–0.8 mm long, sometimes absent in var. tripetala, stipe 12–25 mm long, hairy. Seeds 1–2 per monocarp, obovoid, 10–13 mm by 6–8 mm.

description: Shrub to tree 0.2–5 m tall. Twigs greyish brown to brown, slightly angled in cross-section, glabrous to sparsely hairy. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, oblong to elliptic or broadly elliptic, (4.5–)8–18 cm by (1.5–)3–7 cm, base rounded or slightly acute, apex obtuse to acuminate, the acumen 3–15 mm long, glabrous above, glabrous or with sparse hairs on midrib below, midrib plane to slightly sunken above, secondary veins 6–10 per side; petioles 5–12(–20) mm long. Inflorescences terminal or leaf-opposed, 1–2-flowered, plants sometimes cauliflorous, peduncles 1–5 mm long; pedicels 4–6 mm long; buds ovoid. Sepals broadly ovate or rounded-ovate, 2–2.5 mm long, apex rounded. Outer petals white, ovate, 7.5–13 mm by 4.5–6 mm, apex obtuse or acute, concave, thickened apically, erect or reflexed at apex, sparsely hairy outside, glabrous inside. Inner petals white, elliptic, oblong or obovate, 7–12 mm by 3–4.5 mm, apex acute to obtuse, concave on upper part of inner side, erect or reflexed at apex, glabrous on both sides. Stamens 15–30, oblong, 4–5 mm long; staminodes absent. Carpels 2–6, ovaries oblong or ovoid-oblong, 1.7–2.5 mm long. Fruit of 1–4 monocarps borne on a pedicel 4–6 mm long. Monocarps brown to blackish brown at maturity, 2.3–3 by 0.6–0.8 cm, hairy, with a persistent curved or straight apical beak 2–5 mm long, stipe 1.5–2.5 cm long. Seeds obovoid, 8–12 mm by 5–6 mm.

description: Evergreen, semi-deciduous, or deciduous trees or shrubs, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs (in species occurring in Thailand). Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, base symmetrical, cuneate to rounded, midrib plane or slightly sunken above, secondary venation eucamptodromous or brochidodromous, conspicuous or not, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences terminal, leaf-opposed, or extra-axillary, 1–5-flowered, plants sometimes cauliflorous, pedicellar bract one, attached near pedicel base, caducous, minute, triangular. Flowers hermaphroditic, narrowly ovoid to ovoid or subglobose, rarely deltoid or subcordiform, in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, free, broadly ovate to ovate-triangular with acute apex, much shorter than outer petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, inner whorl of petals sometimes reduced or absent, valvate or imbricate, free or connate in a ring at base, ovate, narrowly ovate, or narrowly oblong, sometimes with a laterally flattened wing, basally concave. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex capitate, truncate, or apiculate. Carpels many, partially connate at base, stigmas clavate, tuberculate; ovule 1(–2) per ovary, basal. Receptacle conical or hemispherical. Fruits pseudosyncarpous, composed of fleshy receptacle and fleshy separate carpels secondarily grown together, pseudosyncarp ovoid to nearly globose, usually glabrescent and sometimes glaucous, surface divided into areoles representing the monocarp apices, these ornamented with knobs, bulges, or prickles, or less often smooth, monocarp bases sessile; pericarp juicy, white to orange and aromatic when fresh, thick, leathery or woody when dried. Seeds numerous per pseudosyncarp, one per monocarp, smooth, glabrous, perichalazal ring indistinct on surface, not raised or sunken, arillate ring encircling the micropyle usually present, endosperm ruminations lamellate, peg-shaped, or spiniform.</br></br>About 100 species with distinctive pseudosyncarpous fruits, most Neotropical with a few native to tropical Africa; 5 species have been introduced to Thailand, where they are cultivated for their edible fruits and have become naturalised in some areas.

description: Shrub or tree to 15 m tall, sometimes with buttresses; bark greyish brown to light brown, slightly rugose. Twigs light brown, reddish brown or grey, glabrous, lenticellate, shoot tip densely covered with golden brown hairs. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, elliptic or ovate, 7–18 by 5–8.5 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex acute, obtuse, or short-acuminate, the acumen 10–15 mm long, glossy green and glabrous above, light green and glabrous below, secondary veins brochidodromous, 7–12 per side, conspicuous above; petioles 10–25 mm long, glabrous. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or extra-axillary, 1-flowered, peduncle up to 20 mm long, pedicels 15–20 mm long, glabrous; buds ovoid or subglobose. Sepals light green, broadly ovate to ovate-triangular, 3–5 mm long, acute, both sides glabrous. Petals in two whorls of 3, free, cream to yellowish cream, red or purple toward the base inside. Outer petals fleshy, valvate, broadly ovate, 15–30 by 13–25 mm, base cordate, apex acute to acuminate, glabrous outside, minutely puberulent inside. Inner petals slightly thinner than outer petals, valvate, ovate or ovate-elliptic, 15–25 by 7–15 mm, base incurved-cuneate, apex acute to slightly obtuse, glabrous on both surfaces. Stamens numerous, oblong, 3–4 mm long, anther locules unequal, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels numerous, linear or oblong, ca 3 mm long, glabrous. Receptacle conical or hemispherical. Pseudosyncarp borne on a pedicel up to 30 mm long, yellow when mature, ovoid, 5–12 by 5–8 cm, smooth, glossy and glabrous, with faint reticulate pattern formed by monocarp boundaries. Seeds ovoid, obovoid or ellipsoid, 11–15 by ca 10 mm, pale brown to brown, shiny.

description: Tree up to 15 m tall; bark (dark) greyish brown, rugose. Twigs (dark) brown, glabrous, lenticellate, shoot tip densely covered with golden brown hairs. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, elliptic, oblong-elliptic, or (narrowly) obovate-oblong, 13–27 by 5–12 cm, base slightly cuneate, apex acuminate, the acumen 10–20 mm long, glossy green and glabrous above, pale green and pubescent to glabrescent below, secondary veins 11–16 per side, more or less eucamptodromous, conspicuous and distinctly parallel; petioles 5–10 mm long, thinly pubescent or glabrescent. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or extra-axillary, 1–2(–5)-flowered, peduncle 15–25 mm long, pedicels 20–35 mm long, pubescent; buds deltoid or obcordate. Sepals broadly triangular, 3–5 mm long, acute, pubescent. Petals valvate, connate in a ring at base, light yellow at maturity. Outer petals thick, fleshy, with an obovate-oblong wing-like dorsal appendage, 15–25 by ca 10 mm, apex round, pubescent. Inner petals small, scale-like. Stamens numerous, oblong, ca 1 mm long, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels numerous, oblong, ca 2.5 mm long, ovaries sericeous. Receptacle slightly elevated, ca 3 mm in diam., 1 mm high. Pseudosyncarp greenish yellow when mature, spherical, ellipsoid or ovoid, 7–20 by 6–20 cm, with areoles marked by thick hexagonal or conical protuberances ending in a brown to black fleshy point. Seeds ovoid or ellipsoid, 9–12 by 6–8 mm, dark brown to black, shiny.

description: Tree up to 10 m tall; bark blackish or greyish brown, rugose. Twigs brown, glabrous, lenticellate, shoot tip densely covered with golden brown hairs. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, elliptic, oblong-elliptic, obovate-oblong to ovate-elliptic, 6–18 by 2.5–7 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex acute or short-acuminate, the acumen 1–2 mm long, glossy green and glabrous above, pale green and slightly hairy below, secondary veins 6–13 per side, brochidodromous, not conspicuous above; petioles 4–15 mm long, glabrous. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or extra-axillary, 1–2(–3)-flowered, plants occasionally cauliflorous, peduncle 2–5 mm long, woody, pedicels 10–20 mm long, pubescent; buds ovoid or subglobose. Sepals ovate-elliptic to ovate-triangular, 3–5 mm long, acute, outside pubescent, inside glabrous. Petals in two whorls of 3, free, greenish yellow to yellow. Outer petals valvate, thick, fleshy, broadly ovate, 30–50 by 25–45 mm, base cordate, apex acute to acuminate, outside rough and pilose, inside smoother and finely pubescent. Inner petals valvate or slightly imbricate, slightly thinner than the outer petals, pale yellow to yellow, ovate or ovate-elliptic, 20–45 by 17–40 mm, base cuneate, apex obtuse, both sides pubescent. Stamens numerous, narrowly cuneate, 4–5 mm long, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels numerous, linear or oblong, ca 5 mm long, pubescent. Receptacle conical or hemispherical. Pseudosyncarp borne on a pedicel up to 30 mm long, pale green when mature, ellipsoid or ovoid and often asymmetrical or curved, 7–35 by 6–20 cm, areoles marked by a distinct curved prickle. Seeds ovoid or ellipsoid, 14–17 by 8–10 mm, brown to dark brown, shiny.

description: Tree 3–8 m tall; bark brown to greyish brown, slightly rugose. Twigs brown, glabrescent, lenticellate, shoot tip pubescent. Leaves chartaceous, narrowly oblong to narrowly ovate, 6–30 by 2–7 cm, base cuneate to obtuse and slightly decurrent onto petiole, apex acuminate, the acumen 10–20 mm long, glabrous above, glabrous or with some short hairs along veins below, secondary veins 9–18 per side, more or less eucamptodromous, conspicuous and parallel; petioles 6–15 mm long, glabrous or slightly pubescent. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or internodal, 1–4-flowered, peduncle 2–5 mm long, woody, pedicels 10–25 mm long, slightly pubescent; buds narrowly ovoid. Sepals ovate, 2–3 mm long, outside pubescent, inside glabrous. Petals valvate. Outer petals greenish yellow outside and pale yellow with a dark-red or purple spot inside at the base, fleshy, narrowly oblong to narrowly ovate, 15–25 by 6–10 mm, outside puberulent, inside glabrous. Inner petals absent. Stamens numerous, oblong, 1–1.4 mm long, anther connective apex subtruncate. Carpels numerous, 1–1.5 mm long, ovate, villous. Receptacle conical or hemispherical. Pseudosyncarp reddish brown to purplish when ripe, spherical to ovoid, 5–16 cm in diam., areoles flat, separated by ridges that give fruit a reticulate surface. Seeds ovoid or ellipsoid, 14–20 by 8–10 mm, dark brown to black, smooth.

description: Deciduous tree or shrub up to 7 m tall; bark brown to dark brown, thin, smooth to slightly rugose. Twigs brown, glabrescent, lenticellate, shoot tip pubescent. Leaves chartaceous, elliptic, oblong to narrowly elliptic or narrowly ovate, 8–15 by 3.5–7 cm, base cuneate, rounded or obtuse, apex acute to obtuse, glabrous above, glabrous or sparsely hairy below, secondary veins more or less eucamptodromous, 8–15 per side, conspicuous above; petioles 4–16 mm long, glabrous. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or internodal, 1–3-flowered, peduncle 2–3 mm long, woody, pedicels 10–30 mm long, glabrous; buds narrowly ovoid. Sepals ovate, 1.5–3 mm, outside pubescent, inside glabrous. Petals valvate, free. Outer petals greenish yellow outside and pale yellow with a dark red or purple spot inside at the base, fleshy, narrowly oblong to narrowly ovate, 15–35 by 5–8 mm, outside puberulent, inside glabrous. Inner petals absent or reduced to acute scales. Stamens numerous, oblong, ca 1 mm long, anther connective apex subtruncate. Carpels numerous, ovate or sometimes oblong, 1–1.5 mm long, villous. Receptacle conical or hemispherical. Pseudosyncarp yellowish or purplish when mature, spherical to ovoid, 7–10 cm in diam., pruinose, areoles rounded, convex, separated by deep grooves. Seeds ovoid or ellipsoid, 10–15 by 6–9 mm, dark brown to black.

description: Evergreen woody climbers, sometimes bearing thorns arising on axillary shoots, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves membranous to coriaceous, base symmetrical or asymmetrical, cuneate, rounded or decurrent on petiole, midrib raised or plane above, secondary venation brochidodromous to weakly brochidodromous, tertiary venation reticulate, rarely subpercurrent. Inflorescences leaf-opposed, 1–many-flowered, floral buds sometimes remaining dormant for a prolonged period, peduncles often recurved and laterally compressed to form hooks (sometimes reduced), with distal branches bearing the flowers arising from them. Flowers hermaphroditic, ovoid in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, free, usually much shorter than the petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, subequal, divided into a laminar, triquetrous, or terete blade and a concave claw, the latter connivent over the stamens and carpels, blades (if laminar) elliptic, obovate, ovate, lanceolate, deltate, rhombic or linear, outer petal claw densely puberulent outside but glabrous inside, inner petals coherent and abscising as a single unit. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex apiculate or truncate. Carpels 2 to many, stigmas cylindrical, rarely clavate or fan-shaped; ovules 2 per ovary, basal, collateral. Receptacle flattened or slightly hemispherical. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, few to many, ellipsoid, obovoid, or ovoid, glabrous or pubescent, smooth or wrinkled, stipitate or sessile; pericarp thick, leathery when dried, or thin, membranous when dried. Seeds basal and collateral, 1–2 per monocarp, ellipsoid (if 1 per monocarp) or plano-convex (if 2 per monocarp), smooth or wrinkled, glabrous, black to brown, perichalazal ring raised or sunken, aril rudimentary, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>A Palaeotropical genus of climbers with peduncular hooks, comprising about 110 species from Africa to Australia, represented in Thailand by 20 species, one, Artabotrys hexapetalus (L. f.) Bhandari, is a widely cultivated introduction.

description: Climber to 20 m tall, sometimes with thorns. Twigs sparsely puberulent, becoming glabrous, outer layer non-flaking. Leaves chartaceous, oblong-lanceolate, oblong-elliptic, or narrowly ovate, 6.5–12.5 by 2.5–4.3 cm, base decurrent on petiole or cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces except for scattered appressed hairs on the midrib below, secondary veins 8–10 per side, tertiary venation reticulate; petioles 3–6 mm long. Inflorescences 1–4-flowered, distal branches arising from peduncular hook short, pedicels 5–6 mm long, sparsely puberulent. Sepals ovate, 6–9 by 5–8 mm, apex acute or obtuse, puberulent on both surfaces. Petals yellow in vivo, puberulent, blades laminar. Outer petals 25–30 mm long, 3–4 mm wide at base, 6–15 mm wide at midpoint, blades elliptic to obovate, apex acute to obtuse; inner petals 20–25 mm long, 2–3 mm wide at base, 6–10 mm wide at midpoint, blades elliptic to obovate, apex acute to obtuse. Stamens 1–2 mm long, anther connective apex apiculate. Carpels ca 20, ca 2.5 mm long. Fruit of up to 17 monocarps borne on a subglabrous pedicel 6–10 mm long. Monocarps drying brownish black, obovoid, 1.8–2 by 1.1–1.5 cm, verruculose, glabrous, apex with a beak ca 1 mm long, base contracted into a stipe 3–4 mm long. Seeds light brown, 14–15 by 8–10 mm, slightly rough.

description: Climber (height unknown). Twigs glabrous, outer layer flaking. Leaves chartaceous to coriaceous, oblong-ovate to oblong-elliptic, 21–33 by 7.3–13.5 cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex acuminate, glabrous above, glabrous to sparsely appressed-pubescent below, secondary veins 11–15 per side, tertiary venation faintly subpercurrent; petioles 6–11 mm long. Inflorescences 1–25-flowered, distal branches arising from peduncular hook elongate (up to 6 cm long), pedicels 15–22 mm long, sparsely puberulent. Sepals broadly ovate, 5–6 by 5–6 mm, apex acute, sparsely puberulent below, glabrous above. Petals cream in vivo, puberulent, blades laminar. Outer petals 16–23 mm long, 7–8 mm wide at base, 6–10 mm wide at midpoint, blades ovate, apex acute. description: Climber to 20 m tall. Twigs glabrous, outer layer usually unbroken, sometimes flaking. Leaves coriaceous, broadly elliptic, rarely ovate, 9–19.5 by 4–8.7 cm, base often rounded, sometimes cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces, secondary veins 7–10 per side, tertiary venation reticulate; petioles 5–15 mm long. Inflorescences 3–5-flowered, distal branches arising from peduncular hook short to medium (up to 1.5 cm long), pedicels 10–20 mm long, glabrous. Sepals ovate, 3–4 by 2–3 mm wide, apex acute, sparsely puberulent outside, glabrous inside. Petals light maroon in vivo, densely puberulent, blades laminar. Outer petals 18–20 mm long, ca 5 mm wide at base, 4–7 mm wide at midpoint, blades ovate, apex acute. Inner petals 15–18 mm long, ca 3 mm wide at base, ca 2 mm wide at midpoint, blades lanceolate, apex acute. Stamens 1–2 mm long, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels ca 10, ca 2 mm long. Fruit of 6–8 monocarps borne on a glabrous pedicel 12–25 mm long. Monocarps drying brown-black, ellipsoid, 3–4 by 1.5–2 cm, slightly verruculose, glabrous, apex with a beak ca 3 mm long, base contracted into a stipe 1–3 mm long. Seeds brown-black, 20–25 by 10–15 mm, rough.

description: Evergreen or deciduous trees or shrubs, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous, elliptic, ovate to sub-rotund, often asymmetrical at base, midrib raised on both sides, more prominent below, secondary veins somewhat parallel, brochidodromus, tertiary venation more or less percurrent. Inflorescences axillary, leaf-opposed, or internodal, 1–6-flowered, fascicled or short-pedunculate. Flowers hermaphroditic, petals separating early in development. Sepals 3(–4), valvate, connate at very base or free, much shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, rarely up to 24, valvate, free, oblong, lanceolate to linear, subequal or inner petals slightly smaller, veins prominent. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex conical. Carpels many; ovules up to 4 per ovary, biseriate. Receptacle slightly convex, sometimes with slightly concave apex. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, ellipsoid, ovoid or subglobose, glabrous, smooth, stipe articulated at the apex; pericarp thin, membranous when dried. Seeds attached laterally in 2 rows, several per monocarp, ellipsoid, flattened, smooth, glabrous, brown, perichalazal ring raised or not visible, arillate, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>A genus of 2 species known for its fragrant flowers, distributed across tropical Asia to NE Australia; both species are present in Thailand, and Cananga odorata is widely cultivated.

description: Deciduous tree to 25 m tall; branches more or less horizontal. Twigs shallowly striate, tomentose, sometimes with small pale raised lenticels. Inflorescences internodal on short, leafy, axillary branches, 1–3-flowered, pendulous, pedicels 15–20 mm long, tomentose. Sepals 3, triangular-ovate, 10–12 by 5–10 mm, tomentose on both sides, spreading, reflexing and folding back at anthesis. Petals 6, in two whorls of 3, green, turning yellow, with red blotch at base inside. Outer petals oblong-lanceolate, 30–50 by (5–)8–15 mm, narrowed at base, with several distinct straight longitudinal veins, tomentose on both sides. Inner petals similar in size to outer petals, or slightly narrower. Stamens linear-oblong, 3–3.5 mm long, anther connective apex conical, pubescent. Carpels ca 4 mm long, glabrous. Fruit of up to 25 monocarps borne on a pedicel up to 20 mm long. Monocarps green, turning dark blue, ripening blackish, subglobose or ellipsoid, (1.2–)1.5–2 cm long by 1–1.3 cm, glaucous, glabrous, somewhat torulose when dried, stipe up to 15 mm long. Seeds 2–4, ellipsoid, flattened, 7–8 mm long by 4–5 mm, brown.

description: Evergreen trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves usually coriaceous, elliptic or oblong, base cuneate to rounded, symmetrical, midrib raised above, secondary venation brochidodromous, tertiary venation percurrent. Inflorescences supra-axillary, 1–4-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, conical or ovoid in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, much shorter than petals, free (in Thai species) or connate. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, linear, oblong, narrowly-oblong or elliptic, (sub-)equal in length (outer petals sometimes slightly longer than inner), broad at base but constricted above and enclosing reproductive organs. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate, dilated. Carpel 1, glabrous; stigma peltate; ovules many per ovary, (1–)2–3(–4)-seriate. Receptacle variably conical with concave apex. Fruit a single indehiscent monocarp, globose, ovoid, or cylindrical, sometimes with constriction between seeds, glabrous, smooth or verrucose, stipe absent or short and inconspicuous; pericarp 2.5–9.1 mm thick. Seeds attached laterally in (1–)2–3(–4) rows, several to numerous per monocarp, ovoid, flattened, glabrous, shiny, smooth or wrinkled, light to deep brownish, perichalazal ring raised, aril absent, endosperm ruminations spiniform.</br></br>Seven species of large canopy trees, the fruit from a single carpel, distributed throughout tropical Asia; 3 species are known from Thailand.

description: Tree to 33 m tall. Young branches sparsely pubescent, becoming glabrous. description: Evergreen small trees or rarely climbers, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to coriaceous, often glaucous below, base (slightly) attenuate, cordate or rounded, symmetrical, midrib plane or slightly sunken above, secondary venation brochidodromous, tertiary venation percurrent. Inflorescences axillary, 1-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, conical in bud. Sepals 3, much shorter than outer petals, valvate, free. Petals in one (outer) whorl of (2–)3, valvate, free, triangular, ovate, elliptic or lanceolate, apically connivent forming a mitriform dome over reproductive organs, creating a pyramidal floral chamber, often with very small basal apertures between petals, inner petals absent. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective truncate, rounded or apiculate. Carpels numerous, stigmas discoid or bilobed, ovaries densely hairy; ovules 1 to many per ovary, lateral. Receptacle shallowly conical with flat apex. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, moniliform (≥ 2-seeded) or ellipsoid (1-seeded), glabrous to densely hairy, smooth, stipitate; pericarp thin, membranous when dried. Seeds attached laterally, up to 8 per monocarp, globose or ellipsoid, glabrous, yellow, red or brown, perichalazal ring plane to slightly raised, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>About 30 species, throughout tropical and subtropical Asia, the flower petals remaining appressed at maturity; 12 species in Thailand.

description: Tree to 10 m tall. Young branches densely hairy. Leaves subcoriaceous, elliptic to oblong, 12–23 by 4.5–7.5 cm, base slightly cordate, apex acute, glabrous above, sparsely hairy and glaucous below; midrib glabrous or sparsely hairy above, densely hairy below, secondary veins 10–15 pairs, slightly impressed above; petioles 3.5–6.5 mm long, densely hairy. Flowers on young growth, pedicels 16–55(–90) mm long, sparsely hairy. Sepals 1.5–4 by 2–3.5 mm. Petals yellow, lanceolate, 40–95 by 11–20(–35) mm, length/width ratio 2.5–5.2, spirally twisted, chartaceous, glabrous adaxially, sparsely hairy abaxially; floral chamber 5.5–8 mm long (10–15% of petal length). Stamens 100–110, anther connective apex truncate; pollen verrucate. Carpels 20–25, stigmas glabrous. Fruit pedicels 12–80 mm long, sparsely hairy. Monocarps 5–22, red, 1.3–4.4 by 0.45–0.7 cm, ellipsoid (1-seeded) or moniliform (≥ 2-seeded), sparsely hairy; constrictions 1.6–3 mm wide (25–55% of monocarp width), stipe 4.5–7 mm long, sparsely hairy. Seeds 1–5, 6–9 by 5–6.5 mm, length/width ratio 1.2–1.6, ellipsoid.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Tree to 5 m tall. Young branches sparsely hairy. Leaves chartaceous, elliptic to oblong, 12.5–17 by 3.5–5.5 cm, base slightly cordate, apex acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces, glaucous below; midrib glabrous above, sparsely hairy below, secondary veins 8–14 pairs, plane or impressed above; petioles 5–7.5 mm long, sparsely hairy. Flowers on young growth, pedicels 46–48 mm long, sparsely hairy. Sepals 2–4 by 2.5–3 mm. Petals yellow, ovate with broadly acute or obtuse apex, 16–30 by 11–15 mm, length/width ratio 1.5–2.1, not twisted, chartaceous, glabrous adaxially, sparsely to densely hairy abaxially; floral chamber ca 6 mm long (20–40% of petal length). Stamens ca 130, anther connective apex truncate; pollen echinate. Carpels ca 11, stigmas sparsely hairy apically. Fruit pedicels 22–63 mm long, sparsely hairy. Monocarps 9–14, red, 2.5–6.5 by 0.65–0.75 cm, ellipsoid (1-seeded) or moniliform (≥ 2-seeded), sparsely hairy; constriction 2–2.5 mm wide (25–35% of monocarp width), stipe 6.5–9.5 mm long, sparsely hairy. Seeds 1–4, 13–16 by 6–7 mm, length/width ratio 1.8–2.5, ellipsoid.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Evergreen trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs, rarely stellate. Leaves chartaceous-subcoriaceous to subcoriaceous, narrowly elliptic, elliptic or elliptic-oblong, base wedge-shaped, obtuse, rounded or subcordate, symmetrical, midrib sunken above, secondary venation rather conspicuous, tertiary venation percurrent. Inflorescences axillary or from axils of fallen leaves, 1–many-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, globose to ellipsoid in bud, petals separating late in development. Sepals 3, valvate or imbricate, free, slightly overlapping at the base, or connate, much shorter than petals, persistent in fruit. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, heart-shaped, ovate or oblong, the inner petals slightly smaller than the outer petals. Stamens 9–11, 14 or 50–56, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels 1–2, stigmas enlarged and more or less peltate; ovules 3–10, lateral, uniseriate or biseriate. Receptacle flat to elevated. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, subglobose to more or less cylindrical, often wrinkled when dried, sometimes coarsely constricted (probably only when dried), densely hairy, nearly smooth to weakly rough, apex rounded; pericarp thick and woody when dried; sessile or short-stipitate (with apical abscission). Seeds 2 to 9 per monocarp, in one or two rows, flattened-ellipsoid or ellipsoid, flattened-D-shaped or D-shaped, more or less brown when dried, surface transversely striate, perichalazal ring nearly plane to raised, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>A tropical Asian genus of 3 species in the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra; represented in Thailand by 1 species.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Dendrokingstonia  . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 16. Part 1, 2022. Pg. 77. Accessed 2024-06-07

description: Evergreen tree to 15(–20) m tall. Twigs sparsely appressed-puberulous. Leaves narrowly elliptic, elliptic or elliptic-oblong, 7.3–18.2 by 2.2–6 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse, subacute to caudate-acuminate, glabrous above, (almost) glabrous below, secondary veins 6–11 per side, prominent below. Inflorescences 1-flowered, pedicels 4–5.2 mm long, each bearing 2 to 3 bracts mostly placed near base. Sepals connate from the base to more or less the midpoint, broadly ovate(-triangular), 1.7–2 mm long. Petals more or less cream-yellow, subcoriaceous-carnose; outer petals ovate to slightly heart-shaped, 5.1–6.2 by 4.1–5.5 mm, base sometimes slightly saccate; inner petals ovate, 5–6.1 by 3.1–3.5 mm, base slightly saccate. Stamens 50–56, 1–1.3 mm long. Carpels 2, appressed-tomentose or tomentose. Receptacle elevated, apex slightly sunken, truncated cone-shaped. Fruit of up to 2 monocarps. Monocarps yellowish brown, irregularly short-cylindrical, 5.9–6.7 by 4.5–5 cm, slightly rough, short-stipitate (with apical abscission), stipe woody, 3–6 by 7–10 mm. Seeds in two rows, up to ca 9 per monocarp, flattened-ellipsoid to flattened D-shaped, 32–36 by 23–24 mm.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Evergreen woody climbers or scandent shrubs, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves membranous to subcoriaceous, often glaucous below, usually oblong, lanceolate, or elliptic, symmetrical with a pair of linear marginal glands at base, midrib sunken or plane, secondary veins somewhat parallel, curving toward the margin but not clearly brochidodromous, tertiary venation percurrent or reticulate. Inflorescences supra-axillary, leaf-opposed, or extra-axillary, rarely axillary or terminal, 1-flowered (in Thai species). Flowers hermaphroditic, petals separating early in development. Sepals 3, much shorter than petals, valvate, free. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, lanceolate, elliptic, or oblong, occasionally oblanceolate to obovate, often undulate along the margins, outer petals slightly longer and wider than inner petals, venation raised or impressed, base of inner petals tightly compressed and enclosing reproductive organs. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate or rounded. Carpels numerous, stigmas globose or clavate; ovules up to 8, attached laterally in a single row. Receptacle cushion-shaped. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, cylindrical, moniliform (≥ 2 seeds) or ellipsoid (1 seed), glabrous or pubescent, smooth, stipitate; pericarp thin, membranous when dried. Seeds attached laterally in a single row, up to 8 per monocarp, smooth, glabrous, brown, perichalazal ring plane, indistinct, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>About 30 species of woody climbers, distinguished by basal leaf glands and moniliform monocarps, distributed throughout tropical Asia to N Australia. For Thailand we recognise 7 species. Desmos chinensis is widely cultivated for its fragrant flowers.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Woody climber or scandent shrub to 8 m high. Twigs appressed-pubescent to glabrate. Leaves chartaceous, rarely subcoriaceous, often glaucous below, oblong to broadly lanceolate, 4.5–15.5 by 2–6.5 cm, 1.9–3.2 times as long as wide, base rounded, truncate, or subcordate, apex acuminate, glabrate above, sparsely appressed-pubescent to glabrate below, secondary veins 7–14 per side, tertiary venation weakly percurrent; petioles 3–7(–10) mm long, glabrate. Inflorescences supra-axillary to internodal, pedicels green to purplish red in vivo, 17–45(–70) mm long, sparsely pubescent to glabrate with 1 linear to lanceolate bract 3–7(–10.5) mm long near or just below the midpoint. Sepals spreading to slightly reflexed, with apex sometimes recurved at maturity, lanceolate, 4–6(–11) mm long, apex acute. Petals yellow, sometimes reddish at the base, membranous, oblong-lanceolate to elliptic, acute to gradually obtuse, margin undulate, venation raised; outer petals 24–73(–95) by 7–18 mm; inner petals (16–)22–50 by 3–11 mm, with basal claw ca 2.5 mm wide. Stamens clavate, 0.8–1.2 mm long, anther connective apex truncate, glabrous. Carpels with ovaries oblong, sericeous, stigmas globose, glabrous. Fruit of up to ca 30 monocarps borne on a pedicel 24–53(–61) mm long, sepals not persistent. Monocarps red to black, moniliform, 0.6–5 by 0.4–0.7 cm, segments subglobose to ellipsoid (6–9 by 5–7 mm), smooth to slightly verrucose, sparsely hairy to glabrate, apiculate, base rounded, contracted into a stipe 4–15 by 0.7–2 mm. Seeds up to 8, commonly 4–6, ellipsoid to oblong-ellipsoid, 5–8 by 4–6 mm.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Woody climber to 20 m high. Twigs densely pubescent, with erect brown to rusty hairs ca 0.4–1.1 mm long, eventually glabrate. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, narrowly oblong, narrowly oblong-elliptic, or lanceolate, 9.2–12.8 by 2.7–4.5 cm, 2.8–3.5 times as long as wide, base cordate to subcordate, occasionally truncate, apex attenuate to an acute tip, glabrous except for the dense and persistent hairs along the midrib above, densely erect-pubescent below, secondary veins 10–13 per side, conspicuous below, tertiary venation weakly percurrent; petioles 4–9 mm long, erect-pubescent. Inflorescences supra-axillary, pedicels green in vivo, 19–57 mm long, densely erect-hairy, with 1 linear to lanceolate bract 3.5–7 mm long near or slightly beyond the midpoint. Sepals spreading at anthesis, lanceolate, 6–10.5 mm long, apex obtuse to acute. Petals pale yellow, membranous to chartaceous, oblanceolate or obovate, acute, margin slightly undulate, venation raised; outer petals 37–64 by 13–24 mm; inner petals lanceolate, 37–48 by 5.5 mm, with a basal claw ca 2.5 mm wide. Stamens and carpels not examined. Fruit of up to 20 monocarps borne on a pedicel 30–35 mm long and ca 1.5 mm thick at midpoint, sepals not persistent, bract persistent or deciduous. Monocarps red to black, moniliform, (0.7–)1.9–2.7 by 0.5–0.6 cm, segments broadly ellipsoid to subglobose (6.5–8 by 5–6 mm), verrucose, erect-pubescent, apex beaked, base contracted into a stipe 2.5–4 by ca 2 mm. Seeds up to 4, broadly ellipsoid, 5.5–8.4 by 5–6 mm.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Woody climber to 10 m high, rarely a scandent shrub. Twigs glabrous, lenticellate. Leaves chartaceous, lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate-oblong, 10.4–15.3 by 2.7–3.8 cm, 3.7–4.1 times as long as wide, base rounded, apex attenuate to an acute tip or acuminate, the acumen 6–12 mm long, glabrous except for scattered hairs along midrib above, glabrous and somewhat glaucous below, secondary veins 14–17 per side, tertiary venation reticulate; petioles 3–7 mm long, with scattered hairs. Inflorescences supra-axillary, rarely axillary or internodal, pedicels green in vivo, 45–90 mm long, glabrous, with 1 linear bract ca 2.2 mm long attached near the pedicel midpoint. Sepals spreading to slightly reflexed, lanceolate, ca 5 mm long, acute. Petals pale orange with a blotch of maroon at the base, chartaceous, lanceolate to narrowly oblong, acute, margin flat, venation flat, indistinct; outer petals ca 25 mm long; inner petals ca 15 mm long. Stamens and carpels not examined. Fruit of up to 11 monocarps borne on a pedicel 17–72 mm long and ca 1 mm thick at midpoint, sepals not persistent, bract persistent. Monocarps moniliform, (0.7–)1.9–2.7 by 0.5–0.6 cm, segments subglobose to ellipsoid (6.5–8 by 5.7–6 mm), smooth to verrucose, glabrate, apex apiculate, base contracted into a slender stipe 9–17 by 0.8–1.1 mm. Seeds up to 3, broadly ellipsoid, 6–7.5 by 3.7–5.4 mm.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Woody climber to 10 m high. Twigs densely to sparsely short erect-pubescent, the hairs 0.2–0.5 mm long. Leaves membranous to subcoriaceous, obovate, elliptic, or oblanceolate, (5–)9.1–15.5 by (2–)3.5–6.1 cm, 2.5–2.6 times as long as wide, base rounded, occasionally subcordate, apex acuminate, sparsely pubescent to glabrate above, erect-pubescent with the hairs most conspicuous along the midrib and secondary veins below, secondary veins 9–15 per side, tertiary venation percurrent; petioles 4–7 mm long, densely pubescent. Inflorescences supra-axillary or terminal, pedicels green in vivo, 15–40 mm long, densely pubescent, with 1 ovate to lanceolate bract 3–7 mm long near the midpoint. Sepals spreading to slightly reflexed at maturity, lanceolate to ovate, 5–12 mm long, apex acute. Petals yellow, membranous to chartaceous, margin undulate, venation raised; outer petals ovate to obovate, 24–70 by 10–36 mm, acute; inner petals ovate-lanceolate, 26–55 by 15–21 mm, acute, with basal claw 2.5–5 mm wide. Stamens clavate, 1.1–1.5 mm long, anther connective apex truncate, glabrous. Carpels with ovaries oblong, pubescent, stigmas clavate, glabrous. Fruit of up to 30 monocarps borne on a pedicel 11–43 mm long and ca 1.5–2 mm thick at midpoint, sepals rarely persistent. Monocarps black, moniliform, 1–5 by 0.5–0.8 cm, segments ellipsoid (8–11 by 6–7 mm), smooth to finely verrucose, sparsely pubescent, apex a blunt beak, base rounded, contracted into a stipe 3–7 by 1.7–3.5 mm. Seeds up to 6, broadly ellipsoid, 6–9.5 by 5–7 mm.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Desmos dumosus . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 16. Part 1, 2022. Pg. 82. Accessed 2024-06-07

description: Woody climber to 30 m high. Twigs glabrous, lenticellate. Leaves subcoriaceous, occasionally glaucous below, oblong-elliptic to oblanceolate, 6–13 by 3–6 cm, ca 2 times as long as wide, base rounded to cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, the acumen 6–10 mm long, glabrous except for scattered hairs along midrib below, secondary veins 11–15 per side, tertiary venation reticulate; petioles 5–7 mm long, with scattered hairs. Inflorescences axillary, peduncle ca 3 mm long, pedicel diverging obliquely from the peduncle, green in vivo, pedicels 6.5–16 mm long, with 1 ovate bract 1–5.5 mm long attached at or just below the pedicel midpoint. Sepals reflexed, broadly ovate, 3.5–7 mm long, sparsely pubescent, obtuse. Petals greenish yellow to yellow, chartaceous, narrowly oblong-lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, venation plane with surface and indistinct, densely pubescent on both surfaces; outer petals 26–39 by 6.5–13 mm, obtuse; inner petals 17–36 by 4–10 mm, obtuse, with basal claw 3–5 mm wide. Stamens oblong, 0.8–1.3 mm long, anther connective apex truncate, glabrous. Carpels with ovaries 0.6–1.4 mm long, pubescent, stigmas clavate or cylindrical, glabrous. Fruit of up to 25 monocarps borne on a pedicel 9–16 mm long and 1.2–1.9 mm thick at midpoint, sepals persistent. Monocarps red, moniliform, 3.7–3.9 by 0.3–0.8 cm, segments ellipsoid (6.2–8.1 by 5–6.2 mm), smooth, glabrous, apex with a distinct beak, base contracted into a slender stipe 10–22 by 0.9–2 mm. Seeds up to 3(–5), oblong-ellipsoid, 6–12 by 4–7 mm.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Habit unknown. Twigs densely appressed-pubescent to glabrate. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, oblanceolate or oblong, 10–17 by 4–5 cm, 2.9–3.3 times as long as wide, base rounded, apex acuminate, the acumen 7–23 mm long, glabrous above, glabrate below, secondary veins 8–14 per side, tertiary venation weakly percurrent; petioles 4–7 mm long, pubescent. Inflorescences axillary, the peduncle (3.5–)8–10 mm long and densely coppery pubescent, pedicel diverging obliquely from the peduncle, pedicels 9.5–25 mm long, sparsely coppery pubescent, with 1 ovate bract 1.8–3 mm long near the midpoint. Sepals spreading to reflexed, ovate to somewhat triangular, 5–6.9 mm long, acute to acuminate. Petals membranous to chartaceous, lanceolate, apex acute to obtuse, slightly undulate, venation flat to slightly raised; outer petals 45–55 by 8–12 mm; inner petals 45–48 by ca 6 mm, with basal claw 2.8–3.8 mm wide. Stamens oblong, 1.1–1.3 mm long, anther connective apex convex, glabrous. Carpels with ovaries oblong, densely pilose, stigmas capitate, glabrous. Fruit borne on a pedicel ca 21 mm long and ca 2 mm thick at midpoint, sepals not persistent. Monocarp (only one on specimen) moniliform, ca 4 by 0.9–1 cm, segments subglobose (8–10 by 7–10 mm), smooth, glabrate, apex rounded, base contracted into a stipe ca 5 by 3 mm. Seeds 4, probably ellipsoid.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Woody climber or scandent shrub to 5 m high. Twigs loosely appressed-pubescent to glabrate. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, oblong, ovate, or oblong-elliptic, 12.1–23.8 by 5.1–8.2 cm, 1.4–3.4 times as long as wide, base broadly cuneate to rounded, occasionally subcordate, apex acute to short-acuminate, glabrate or with a few hairs along the midrib above, sparsely appressed-pubescent to glabrate and occasionally glaucous below, secondary veins 7–14(–21) per side, tertiary venation weakly percurrent; petioles 7–9 mm long, pubescent. Inflorescences supra-axillary to internodal, pedicels red to purple in vivo, 45–150 mm long, sparsely pubescent with 1 linear bract 1.6–3 mm long near midpoint. Sepals reflexed at maturity, lanceolate or narrowly triangular, 5–9 mm long, usually long-acuminate. Petals yellow, sometimes red at base, coriaceous or slightly fleshy, acute, margin flat, venation impressed; outer petals elliptic, 31–47 by 11–26 mm; inner petals lanceolate, 33–34 by 8–9 mm, with basal claw 2.5–4.5 mm wide. Stamens clavate, 1.1–1.7 mm long, anther connective apex rounded, glabrous. Carpels with ovaries oblong, sericeous, stigmas globose, glabrous. Fruit of up to ca 20 monocarps borne on a pedicel 86–164 mm long, sepals not persistent. Monocarps black, moniliform, 0.8–3.7 by 0.4–0.7 cm, segments subglobose, smooth, sparsely hairy to hairy, apex apiculate, base rounded, contracted into a stipe 10–18 by 0.8–1.7 mm. Seeds up to 6, oblong-ellipsoid, 3–9 by 3–6 mm.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Desmos pedunculosus . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 16. Part 1, 2022. Pg. 86. Accessed 2024-06-07

description: Evergreen small trees or shrubs, primary branching pattern unknown. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, oblanceolate to elliptic, cuneate, short-decurrent, and symmetrical at base, venation indistinct, midrib plane above, secondary veins indistinct, arcuate or diverging at irregular angles, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences terminal, 1–3-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, petals separating early in development. Sepals 3 (in Thai species), valvate or somewhat imbricate, free, shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate or slightly imbricate, free (in Thai species), oblanceolate to panduriform, the outer petals slightly longer and wider than the inner petals. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex depressed-globose. Carpels up to 200, stigmas narrowly oblong, obtuse at the apex; ovules 1–3, uniseriate. Receptacle cushion-shaped. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, ellipsoid, stipe articulated at the apex; pericarp thin, membranous when dried. Seeds attached laterally in 1 row, up to 3 per monocarp, ellipsoid or flattened-ellipsoid, smooth, glabrous, brown and shiny, perichalazal ring slightly raised, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>Nine species in tropical and subtropical Asia, represented in Thailand by a single species. The large number of monocarps with a distinct articulation at the apex of the long stipes characterise the genus.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Disepalum  . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 16. Part 1, 2022. Pg. 87. Accessed 2024-06-07

description: Tree to 10 m tall. Twigs glabrous. Leaves chartaceous, oblanceolate to elliptic, 10.5–14.2 by 4.3–4.7 cm, base cuneate and short-decurrent on petiole, apex acuminate, the acumen 6–10 mm long, glabrous on both surfaces, secondary veins 10–11 per side; petioles 4.5–7 mm long. Inflorescences terminal, 1-flowered, pedicel 19–28 mm long, without bracts; petals separating early in bud. Sepals ovate, chartaceous, 13–15 mm long, obtuse, pubescent. Petals subcoriaceous, pale green, yellow, or pale orange, elliptic, oblanceolate or panduriform, acute to cuspidate, 21–44 by 8–25 mm, inner petals slightly shorter and narrower than outer petals. Stamens oblong, 2 mm long, anther connective apex depressed-globose. Carpels 120–200, ovaries pubescent, narrowly oblong. Receptacle cushion-shaped, 1–2 mm high, 7–8.5 mm in diam. Fruit of up to 100 monocarps borne on a pedicel up to 67 mm long. Monocarps purple, ellipsoid, glabrate, 1.4–2.1 by 0.7–1 cm, smooth, apex rounded or apiculate, stipe articulated at the apex, crimson, 31–44 by 1.3–2.1 mm; pericarp 0.1–0.2 mm thick. Seeds in a single row, up to 3 per monocarp, flattened-ellipsoid, 10–13 mm long, 7.5–8.5 mm wide, chestnut-brown.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Disepalum pulchrum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 16. Part 1, 2022. Pg. 87. Accessed 2024-06-07

description: Evergreen trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of stellate hairs (rarely simple). Leaves papyraceous to coriaceous, elliptic or oblong, base cuneate, rounded or cordate, symmetrical or asymmetrical, midrib plane or sunken above, secondary venation brochidodromous, tertiary venation percurrent. Inflorescences supra-axillary, 1–8-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, ovoid or conical in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, free, (slightly) shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, oblong, linear, ovate, elliptic or lanceolate, (sub-)equal in length, similar in shape, broad at base but constricted above and enclosing reproductive organs. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate, dilated. Carpels (1–)2–32, glabrous or pubescent; stigmas ellipsoid or obconical; ovules many per ovary, 1–2-seriate. Receptacle flat or elongated. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, ovoid, ellipsoid, or cylindrical, sometimes constricted between seeds, glabrous or pubescent, smooth or verrucose; pericarp of variable thickness, leathery or woody; stipes present or absent. Seeds attached laterally in 1–2 rows, few to numerous per monocarp, ovoid, flattened-ovoid, or lenticular, smooth, pitted, or wrinkled, glossy or matt, light to deep brown, perichalazal ring plane or sunken, rarely raised, aril absent (except in D. pruniferus), endosperm ruminations peg-like (sometimes spiniform).</br></br>Twenty-six species, distributed throughout tropical Asia and in the W Pacific; 1 species in Thailand. The Thai species has a monopodial habit with lateral branches resembling compound leaves, the “phyllomorphic ramuli” of Corner (Ann. Bot., n. s., 13: 392, 1949).
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Drepananthus  . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 16. Part 1, 2022. Pg. 89. Accessed 2024-06-07

description: Trees to 30 m tall. Young branches densely pubescent, becoming glabrous. Leaves subcoriaceous, elliptic or oblong, 10.5–42.5 by 6.5–19.5 cm, base rounded or subcordate, slightly oblique, apex acute, rounded or mucronulate, pubescent below, midrib depressed above, secondary veins (10–)14–22 pairs; petioles 9–25.5 mm long. Inflorescences on older branches or trunk, 1–8-flowered, pedicels 7–22.5 mm long, pedicel bracts 5–13 by 2.5–7 mm. Sepals free, 7–15 by 3.5–10.5 mm. Petals ovate or oblong, constricted just above stamens and carpels; outer petals 10.5–16 by 6.5–10.5 mm above constriction, 5–9.5 mm wide below constriction; inner petals 9–16 by 4.5–6.5 mm above constriction. Stamens 109–154, 1.3–2.9 mm long. Carpels 7–13 per flower, hairy; stigmas ellipsoid; ovules 8–18 per carpel, biseriate. Receptacle flat. Monocarps 6–10 per fruit, 16.5–31 by 16–24 mm, ovoid with rounded apex, glabrous, stipe absent (sessile); pericarp 1.3–2.5 mm thick when dried. Seeds ca 10, biseriate, 11.5–15.5 by 7–9 mm, flattened-ovoid, aril ca 1.5 mm long, attached at base, fleshy, bilobed.

description: Evergreen woody climbers, branches often flexuous and wrapping around adjacent supports, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to coriaceous, occasionally glaucous below, elliptic, oblong, or oblanceolate, occasionally ovate or obovate, base symmetrical, cuneate, rounded, or subcordate, midrib plane or sunken above, secondary veins usually conspicuous, parallel and barely joining near leaf margin, tertiary venation weakly to strongly percurrent. Inflorescences terminal, usually leaf-opposed, rarely axillary, 1–20-flowered, pedicels arising from a short common peduncle (fasciculate) or an extended rachis (racemose). Flowers hermaphroditic, ovoid to conical in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, slightly connate at base or free, much shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, lanceolate to ovate, the inner petals slightly shorter, narrower, and more acute than the outer petals, at anthesis the outer petals spreading or reflexed and the inner petals erect with the tips slightly spreading to form a narrow aperture. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex acute to rounded, sometimes tongue-shaped. Carpels 10–20, stigmas narrowly oblong to clavate, truncate, bilobed, or bifurcate at the apex; ovules 2 to many per ovary, biseriate. Receptacle elevated, truncate. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, globose, ellipsoid, obovoid, or oblongoid, glabrous or pubescent, often marked by bumps and ridges, stipitate; pericarp thick, leathery or woody when dried. Seeds attached laterally in 1–2 rows, up to 13 per monocarp, semicircular, wedge-shaped in cross-section, smooth, glabrous, shiny, brown, reddish brown, or black, perichalazal ring not evident, aril absent but a light-coloured ring encircling the micropyle often present, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>A genus of over 60 species, distributed across tropical and subtropical Asia. Twelve species are confirmed for Thailand, but the genus remains poorly known, as the plants are woody climbers flowering in the canopy. Collectors often comment on the sweet fragrance of the flowers.

description: Woody climber to 15 m high. Twigs brown-pubescent, eventually glabrate. Inflorescences terminal on young shoots, eventually leaf-opposed, 1–6-flowered, peduncle ca 1 mm long, pedicels 2–7.5 mm long, bearing 2 bracts up to 5.5 mm long; buds broadly conic-ovoid. description: Woody climber to 10 m high. Twigs rusty appressed-pubescent, eventually glabrate. description: Woody climber. Twigs with dense appressed brown pubescence when young, later glabrate. Sepals triangular-ovate, coriaceous, 3–4 mm long, acute, densely brown-pubescent outside, glabrous inside. Petals yellow to orange-yellow, fleshy, concave at base; outer petals ovate-lanceolate, 14–16 mm by 5–6.5 mm, slightly obtuse, hairy on both surfaces, except glabrous at base inside; inner petals ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, 10–13 mm by 3–4.5 mm, acute, glabrous. description: Woody climber. Twigs initially rusty-pubescent but soon glabrate. description: Woody climber to 20 m high. Twigs dull red-pubescent, eventually glabrate. Leaves subcoriaceous, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, occasionally obovate, 11–15.5 by 4.9–7.4 cm, base rounded, almost subcordate, apex obtuse to acute or short-acuminate, the acumen 2–3 mm long, finely dull red-pubescent to glabrate except for the persistently dull red-pubescent midrib above, sparsely dull red erect-pubescent below, secondary veins 11–17 per side, tertiary venation prominent below; petioles 8–11 mm long, of even thickness from midpoint to leaf blade. Inflorescences terminal or rarely axillary, 6–19-flowered, racemose with an extended rachis 2.5–9 cm long, pedicels 8–13.5 mm long, bearing one bract ca 1.3 mm long; buds ovoid. Sepals narrowly triangular, coriaceous, 1.4–2 mm long, acute, dull red-pubescent. Petals coriaceous to slightly fleshy, yellow; outer petals lanceolate, 10–12.5 by 4.3–5 mm, obtuse; inner petals lanceolate, ca 6 by 2 mm, acuminate. Stamens [ex J.Sinclair] 1–1.3 mm long, anther connective apex oblique and obtuse. Ovaries golden-sericeous, stigmas rodlike. Receptacle short-cylindrical, 1–1.3 mm high, 1.3–1.5 mm in diam. Fruit of up to 8 monocarps borne on a pedicel 15–22 mm long. Monocarps globose, 1.3–3 cm in diam., dull red-pubescent, rough or slightly verrucose, apex rounded, stipe 17–22 [–35, Sinclair, 1955] by 1–2.7 mm; pericarp ca 1 mm thick. Seeds in two rows, dark brown.

description: Woody climber. Twigs reddish brown-pubescent. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, oblong-lanceolate, oblong-obovate, or oblanceolate, 8−28 by 4−10 cm, base broadly cuneate, rounded, or cordate, apex acute to acuminate, the acumen 7−20 mm long, glabrous, densely pubescent on midrib above, reddish brown-tomentose, the hairs densest along the veins, below, secondary veins 17−22 per side, tertiary venation prominent below; petioles 10−20 mm long, of even thickness from midpoint to leaf blade. description: Woody climber. Twigs persistently orange-pubescent. description: Woody climber. Twigs golden to greyish brown-pubescent. Inflorescences terminal, ca 7-flowered, racemose with an extended rachis ca 6 cm long, pedicels 13–22 mm long, each bearing 1 bract 3–6 mm long attached near the pedicel base; buds ovoid, obtuse. Sepals triangular, coriaceous, 2–4.5 mm long, obtuse, coarsely and densely golden brown-pubescent. Petals fleshy; outer petals linear-lanceolate, 18–22 by 5–7 mm, obtuse; inner petals ovate-lanceolate, 8–12 by 3–5 mm, acute. Stamens ca 1.2 mm long, anther connective apex triangular, acute. Seeds in one or two rows, up to 11 per monocarp, flattened-ellipsoid or semicircular and flattened, 12–16 mm by 7.5–10 mm, smooth, shiny, dark brown to black.

description: Woody climber to 20 m high. Twigs finely erect brown-pubescent, eventually glabrous. description: Woody climber to 20 m high. Twigs short brown-pubescent, eventually glabrous. description: Woody climber to 10 m. Twigs densely orange-pubescent, eventually sparsely pubescent to glabrate. description: Evergreen woody climbers or scandent shrubs, rarely shrubs or treelets, often with twigs forming loops around supports, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to coriaceous, frequently glaucous below, base symmetrical with a pair of linear marginal glands near petiole, midrib sunken above, secondary venation conspicuous, tertiary venation percurrent. Inflorescences internodal to leaf-opposed, occasionally supra-axillary, 1(–2)-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, conical in bud. Sepals 3, valvate or rarely imbricate at base, free or sometimes basally connate, much shorter than outer petals, often persistent in fruit. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, outer petals long and narrow, spreading at anthesis, inner petals much shorter than outer petals, connivent to form a pyramidal cone over the stamens and carpels, each petal with a short broad claw. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate to ovoid. Carpels 9–20, stigmas globose or clavate; ovules 1(–2), basal(–lateral). Receptacle conical. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, ellipsoid, oblongoid, or ovoid, smooth or finely verrucose, glabrous or pubescent, stipitate; pericarp thin, membranous when dried. Seed(s) attached basally, 1(–2) per monocarp, often difficult to separate from pericarp, ellipsoid, smooth, glabrous, light brown, perichalazal ring evident as a thin line, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>About 45 tropical Asian species of climbers with basal leaf glands and strong smelling flowers. There are 16 species in the Thai flora.

description: Scandent shrub or woody climber up to 10 m high. Twigs densely rusty short-pubescent to glabrate. Leaves subcoriaceous to coriaceous, somewhat bullate to rugose above, glaucous below, oblong, oblanceolate, or obovate, 12–20 by 5–12 cm, base rounded to cordate, apex acute, acuminate, or mucronate, the acumen 2–10 mm long, glabrate except for pubescent midrib above, pubescent, especially along midrib and secondary veins, below, secondary veins 6–11 per side; petioles 4.5–18 mm long, sunken above, pubescent. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or supra-axillary, 1(–2)-flowered, pedicels 6–10 mm long, somewhat curved, pubescent, with a clasping cordate to reniform bract 5–11.2 mm long attached at pedicel midpoint; buds lanceolate, acute. Sepals valvate, subcoriaceous, ovate, 10–12 mm long, acute, strongly 5-veined, glaucous, pubescent. Petals yellow, coriaceous; outer petals appressed in bud, erect at anthesis, linear-oblong or linear-lanceolate, 17–55 by 5–10 mm, triquetrous (three-angled in cross-section) toward apex, acute, concave on inner base, glaucous and finely rusty- to white-pubescent; inner petals coriaceous, linear-lanceolate, 16.5–35 by 5–7 mm, margins without protrusions at midpoint, apex acuminate, glabrous except hairy along margin distally outside, glabrous inside. Monocarps red to pink-red, ovoid to broadly ellipsoid, 0.7–1.7 by 0.6–1.2 cm, sparsely pubescent, apex obtuse to rounded with an apiculum 0.5–2 mm long, stipe 5–10 by 2.5–3 mm. description: Scandent shrub or woody climber up to 2 m high. Twigs densely brown or dark brown appressed- to spreading-pubescent, eventually moderately pubescent or glabrate. description: Woody climber up to 6 m high. Twigs densely orange to reddish brown-tomentose, eventually glabrate. description: Scandent shrub or treelet up to 3 m tall. Twigs persistently pubescent with short dense erect orangish to reddish brown hairs. Leaves chartaceous to nearly membranous, glaucous below, oblanceolate to obovate, 10.5–16 by 3.8–5.6 cm, base rounded, nearly truncate or subcordate, apex short-acuminate, the broad acumen 4–10 mm long, or sometimes obtuse, glabrous above, spreading-pubescent below, secondary veins 11–20 per side; petioles 3–7 mm long, slightly sunken to flattened above, pubescent. Petals pale yellow to light orange; outer petals separating widely in bud, chartaceous, ligulate, (19–) 27–31 by 7–9 mm, flat toward apex, acute, flat on inner base, pubescent; inner petals elliptic, 10–11.3 by 4–4.5 mm, acute, margins without protrusions at midpoint, pubescent on both surfaces. description: Scandent shrub or woody climber. Twigs initially rusty appressed-pubescent, soon glabrate. description: Treelet or woody climber up to 4 m high. Twigs hispid. Leaves chartaceous to membranous, occasionally slightly glaucous, oblanceolate, oblong-oblanceolate, or obovate, 10–21.6 by 4–8 cm, base irregularly subcordate to cordate, apex acute to acuminate, the narrow acumen 5–18 mm long, glabrous above, hispid below, secondary veins 11–18 per side; petioles 2–5 mm long, flat to slightly sunken above, hispid. Inflorescences supra-axillary to internodal, 1-flowered, pedicels 59–95 mm long, hispid, with a linear to narrowly elliptic bract 2.5–4.5 mm long attached at or just proximal to the pedicel midpoint. Sepals valvate, subcoriaceous, lanceolate, 6–10.6 mm long, acute to long-acuminate, 1-veined, hispid. Petals yellow to brownish yellow, coriaceous; outer petals appressed in bud, slightly spreading at anthesis, linear, 38–81 by 3.5–3.8 mm, triquetrous (three-angled in cross-section) toward apex, caudate, concave on inner base, pubescent; inner petals loosely connivent, lanceolate, 5–10 mm long, caudate to acuminate, glabrous. description: Woody climber up to 7 m high. Twigs glabrous to sparsely tomentose. Leaves membranous to chartaceous, glaucous below, oblanceolate, elliptic, obovate-oblong or obovate, 13.3–28 by 5.8–12 cm, base broadly cuneate, rounded or slightly cordate, apex acuminate, the acumen 6–20 mm long, pubescent when young, eventually glabrate above, glabrate or with short appressed reddish brown hairs below, secondary veins 8–16 per side; petioles 6–15 mm long, deeply sunken above, glabrous. Inflorescences internodal, 1-flowered, pedicels 14–28 mm long, glabrous or covered with sparse appressed reddish brown hairs, with a linear-lanceolate bract 0.9–1.7 mm long attached to basal half of pedicel. Sepals valvate, coriaceous, triangular, 4–6 mm long, without visible venation, pubescent outside, acute. description: Woody climber to 5 m high. Twigs moderately short brown-pubescent, the hairs appressed, eventually glabrate. Leaves chartaceous, paler but not glaucous below, oblong or lanceolate-oblong or oblanceolate, 13–22 by 3.8–7.5 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex acuminate, the acumen (3–)7–20 mm long, appressed-pubescent on both surfaces but denser below, secondary veins 9–12 per side; petioles 8–17 mm long, flattened above, densely pubescent. description: Woody climber or scandent shrub up to 10 m high. Twigs densely short brown-pubescent. description: Evergreen trees, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves papyraceous to coriaceous, attenuate, cuneate or rounded and symmetrical at base, midrib plane or sunken above, secondary venation brochidodromous, tertiary venation reticulate to percurrent. Inflorescences axillary or very slightly internodal on young growth, or from woody tubercles on trunk or main branches, 1(2–4)-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, generally pendent, ovoid to ellipsoid in bud with outer petals often separating before maturity. Sepals 3, valvate, free or sometimes basally connate, shorter than outer petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, ovate, elliptic or lanceolate, outer petals longer than inner petals (rarely subequal), sometimes slightly clawed, inner petals basally clawed with blade much longer than claw, apically connivent over reproductive organs, forming a mitriform dome with 3 lateral apertures. Stamens numerous, anthers septate, connective apex truncate to apiculate. Carpels 4–ca 100, stigmas subulate, fusiform or funnel-shaped, sometimes enlarged; ovules 1–several, basal or lateral. Receptacle triangular at base. Fruits often with sepals persistent, apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, subglobose to ellipsoid, sometimes moniliform, glabrous or pubescent, smooth or bumpy, generally stipitate; pericarp thin, membranous when dried, or thick, leathery or woody when dried. Seeds attached basally, or laterally in one row, 1–3(–10) per monocarp, often surrounded by mucilage, generally round to ellipsoid, smooth or slightly striate, glabrous to densely hairy, perichalazal ring raised, plane, or sunken, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>About 130 species, throughout tropical and subtropical SE Asia and east to the W Pacific; 27 species in Thailand. The voucher specimen for the report of Goniothalamus saigonensis Pierre ex Finet & Gagnep. from Thailand by Craib (1925), Collins 914 from Prachin Buri, could not be located and its identity is unknown. The generic name refers to the angular base of the receptacle.

Flowers paired in large fascicles, at base of trunk, pedicels 15–110 mm long. Sepals 9–13.5 by 6–9 mm, not reflexed, venation indistinct. Outer petals cream-yellow, 12–50 by 9–20 mm, sparsely to densely hairy abaxially, (very densely) woolly adaxially with velutinous basal region facing apertures between inner petals, venation indistinct. Inner petals cream-yellow, 11–17 by 7–9.5 mm, (very densely) hairy abaxially, velutinous adaxially. Stamens 120–320, anther connective apex short- to long-apiculate. Carpels 34–90, ovaries glabrous; stigmas funnel-shaped, glabrous. Fruits with persistent sepals, pedicels 30–130 mm long. Monocarps yellow, pink, red or purple, ellipsoid to obovoid, 1.6–3.5 by 1.3–2.9 cm, smooth, glabrous to sparsely hairy, stipe 2–15 mm long. Seeds 1–2(–3), 15–25 by 10–18 mm, smooth, (sparsely) hairy.

description: Tree to 5 m tall. Young branches subglabrous. Leaves papyraceous, elliptic to obovate, 17–25 by 5–7.5 cm, matt to slightly glossy above, sparsely hairy below, (sub)glabrous above, secondary veins 13–16 pairs, (slightly) impressed above; tertiary venation weakly percurrent, (very) distinct; petioles 8–18 mm long. Flowers solitary, on young growth, pedicels 13–16 mm long. Sepals ca 6 by 9–10 mm, reflexed, venation indistinct. Outer petals greenish yellow, tinged with red basally, ca 29 by ca 22 mm, subglabrous abaxially, glabrous adaxially with essentially glabrous (sparsely hairy towards apex) basal region facing apertures between inner petals, venation distinct. Inner petals pale yellow, 16–17 by 11–12 mm, sparsely hairy abaxially, hairy adaxially. Stamens ca 180, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels ca 18, ovaries glabrous; stigmas fusiform, glabrous, warty. Fruits with persistent sepals, pedicels 16–22 mm long. Monocarps green tinged with purple-pink, subglobose or ellipsoid to elongate, 1.7–5.4 by 1.5–2.4 cm, ± smooth, glabrous, stipe 3–8 mm long. Seeds 1–6, 15–22 by 13–17 mm, smooth to slightly rugulose, hairy.

description: Shrub or tree to 4 m. Young branches glabrous. Leaves chartaceous, elliptic to oblanceolate, 15–40 by 3–13 cm, glabrous on both surfaces (sometimes sparsely pubescent over midrib), secondary veins 15–22 pairs, plane adaxially; tertiary venation percurrent, slightly distinct; petioles 12–22 mm long. Flowers solitary, often on main trunk (cauliflorous), rarely on older branches (ramiflorous), pedicels 10–17 mm long, Sepals 20–30 by 24–35 mm, venation distinct. Outer petals (violet-)pink, green on claw, 25–45 by 14–25 mm, sparsely hairy abaxially (more densely along margins basally), sparsely hairy (more densely apically) adaxially with velutinous basal region facing apertures between inner petals, venation indistinct. Inner petals pale pink, 12–20 by 8–11 mm, densely hairy ab- and adaxially. Stamens numerous, anther connective apex apiculate. Carpels 20–35, ovaries hairy; stigmas subulate, glabrous. Fruits with persistent sepals, pedicels 10–20 mm long, Monocarps (pinkish) red, ellipsoid to ovoid, 0.8–1.5 by 0.7–0.9 cm, smooth, sparsely hairy, apex apiculate, stipe 3–5 mm long. Seeds solitary, otherwise not examined.

description: Tree to 9 m tall. Young branches very sparsely to densely hairy. Leaves papyraceous, (ovate-)elliptic, 10.5–23.5 by 3.5–8.5 cm, matt above, (sub)glabrous below and above, secondary veins 8–17 pairs, ± plane above; tertiary venation reticulate, indistinct or ± distinct; petioles 6–18 mm long. Outer petals yellowish, 7–28 by 3.5–12 mm, (sparsely) hairy ab- and adaxially with velutinous basal region facing apertures between inner petals, venation indistinct. Inner petals pale yellow, 4–11.5 by 2.5–5.5 mm, (sparsely) hairy abaxially, velutinous adaxially. Stamens 24–80, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels 9–15, ovaries (densely) hairy; stigmas funnel-shaped or subulate, glabrous or warty. Fruits with persistent sepals, pedicels 4–8 mm long. Monocarps bright red, subglobose to ellipsoid, 0.85–1.2 by 0.65–0.85 cm, apiculate, smooth, very sparsely hairy, stipe 2–3 mm long. Seeds solitary, 7.5–9.5 by 5.5–8 mm, smooth, glabrous.

description: Tree to 20 m tall. Young branches (very densely) hairy. Inner petals pale yellow, 12–18 by 5–8 mm, (very) densely hairy (except glabrous basal flanges) abaxially, densely hairy (glabrous towards base) adaxially. Stamens 110–220, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels 40–100, ovaries (sub)glabrous; stigmas subulate, (sub)glabrous. Fruits without persistent sepals, pedicels ca 20 mm long. description: Tree to 12 m tall. Young branches (sub)glabrous. description: Shrub or tree to 4 m. Young branches densely appressed-pubescent. Leaves subcoriaceous, (lanceolate-)oblong, 28–50 by 7–16 cm, glabrous below (sparsely hairy over midrib), sparsely pubescent above (densely hairy over veins), secondary veins 32–40 pairs, plane adaxially; tertiary venation percurrent, distinct; petioles 20–30 mm long. Flowers solitary or paired, often on main trunk, rarely on older branches, pedicels 12–18 mm long. Sepals 7–9.5 by 7.5–10 mm, venation indistinct. Outer petals whitish yellow, green on claw, 34–37 by 18–22 mm, moderately hairy abaxially, densely hairy adaxially, venation indistinct. Inner petals pinkish orange to reddish brown, 13–15 by 7–8 mm, sparsely hairy distally abaxially, densely hairy adaxially. Stamens numerous, anther connective apex apiculate. Carpels 11–20, ovaries hairy; stigmas funnel-shaped, hairy. Fruits sometimes with persistent sepals, pedicels 20–25 mm long. Monocarps (obovoid-)ellipsoid, apex apiculate, 2–2.7 by 0.9–1.3 cm, smooth, densely hairy, apex apiculate, stipe 7–15 mm long. Seeds solitary, 13–17 by 8–10 mm, slightly rugose.
